questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II regarding asexual reproductive structures/methods and the organisms in which they are observed, and select the correct combination.

List I (Structure / Method)List II (Organism)
A. Zoospores(i) Sponge
B. Conidia(ii) Chlamydomonas
C. Gemmules(iii) Amoeba
D. Binary fission(iv) Penicillium

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Zoospores
Members of Kingdom Fungi and simple plants such as algae reproduce through special asexual reproductive structures. The most common of these are microscopic motile structures called zoospores, which are characteristic of the green alga Chlamydomonas.

Step 2: Analysis of Conidia
Non-motile asexual spores formed exogenously in chains on branched conidiophores are called conidia, which are commonly observed in the fungus Penicillium.

Step 3: Analysis of Gemmules and Binary Fission
Gemmules are internal asexual reproductive structures found in sponges. Binary fission is a mode of asexual reproduction in single-celled organisms where a cell divides into two halves that rapidly grow into adults, as seen in Amoeba.

Step 4: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: Zoospores with Chlamydomonas, Conidia with Penicillium, Gemmules with Sponge, and Binary fission with Amoeba (A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii)).

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II regarding vegetative propagules and the angiosperms in which they occur, and choose the correct match.

List I (Vegetative Propagule)List II (Plant)
A. Eyes(i) Agave
B. Rhizome(ii) Water hyacinth
C. Bulbil(iii) Potato
D. Offset(iv) Ginger

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In plants, structures capable of giving rise to new offspring without involving two parents are called vegetative propagules. These represent modes of asexual reproduction.

Step 2: Matching Each Propagule to Its Plant
Small plants emerge from the buds (called eyes) present on the tuber of potato. Underground modified stems called rhizomes serve as vegetative propagules in ginger (and banana). Bulbils are fleshy vegetative buds found in Agave. Offsets are horizontal aquatic stem branches that allow rapid vegetative propagation in water hyacinth.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: Eyes with Potato, Rhizome with Ginger, Bulbil with Agave, and Offset with Water hyacinth (A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(ii)).

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II to pair each organism with its approximate life span, and select the correct combination.

List I (Organism)List II (Approximate Life Span)
A. Butterfly(i) 100–150 years
B. Crow(ii) 60 years
C. Crocodile(iii) 1–2 weeks
D. Tortoise(iv) 15 years

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The period from birth to the natural death of an organism represents its life span. Life spans vary widely among organisms and are not necessarily correlated with body size.

Step 2: Matching Each Organism to Its Approximate Life Span
A butterfly has a very short approximate life span of 1–2 weeks. A crow has an approximate life span of 15 years (in contrast to a parrot of similar size, which lives about 140 years). A crocodile has an approximate life span of 60 years, whereas a tortoise has a much longer approximate life span of 100–150 years.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: Butterfly with 1–2 weeks, Crow with 15 years, Crocodile with 60 years, and Tortoise with 100–150 years (A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(ii), D-(i)).

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II regarding organisms and their sexual condition, and select the correct answer.

List I (Organism)List II (Sexual Condition)
A. Chara(i) Unisexual animal
B. Marchantia(ii) Bisexual animal (hermaphrodite)
C. Earthworm(iii) Monoecious plant
D. Cockroach(iv) Dioecious plant

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Organisms that possess both male and female reproductive structures on the same individual are termed bisexual (monoecious or homothallic in plants/fungi, and hermaphrodites in animals). Organisms with male and female reproductive structures on separate individuals are unisexual (dioecious or heterothallic in plants/fungi).

Step 2: Evaluation of Each Organism
Chara bears both the oogonium (female sex organ) and antheridium (male sex organ) on the same plant, making it a monoecious plant. Marchantia bears archegoniophores and antheridiophores on separate thalli, making it a dioecious plant. Earthworm possesses both testes and ovaries in the same body, so it is a bisexual animal (hermaphrodite). Cockroach has separate male and female individuals, making it a unisexual animal.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: Chara as a monoecious plant, Marchantia as a dioecious plant, Earthworm as a bisexual animal (hermaphrodite), and Cockroach as a unisexual animal (A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(ii), D-(i)).

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIONINORGANISMS_MATCHLIST_Q05 - Chromosome numbers in meiocytes and gametes

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II regarding the chromosome numbers in meiocytes (\(2n\)) or gametes (\(n\)) of the listed organisms, and select the correct combination.

List I (Organism and Cell Type)List II (Chromosome Number)
A. Ophioglossum — gamete (\(n\))(i) 23
B. Fruit fly — meiocyte (\(2n\))(ii) 630
C. Human beings — gamete (\(n\))(iii) 78
D. Dog — meiocyte (\(2n\))(iv) 8

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
In diploid organisms, specialised gamete mother cells called meiocytes (\(2n\)) undergo meiosis so that each haploid gamete (\(n\)) receives exactly half the chromosome number of the meiocyte.

Step 2: Verification of Chromosome Numbers
In the fern Ophioglossum, the chromosome number in a gamete (\(n\)) is 630 (corresponding to \(2n = 1260\) in the meiocyte). In the fruit fly, the chromosome number in a meiocyte (\(2n\)) is 8 (with \(n = 4\) in gametes). In human beings, the chromosome number in a gamete (\(n\)) is 23 (half of \(2n = 46\)). In dogs, the chromosome number in a meiocyte (\(2n\)) is 78 (with \(n = 39\) in gametes).

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: Ophioglossum gamete with 630, Fruit fly meiocyte with 8, Human beings gamete with 23, and Dog meiocyte with 78 (A-(ii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(iii)).

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II regarding reproductive phenomena and their corresponding examples, and choose the correct option.

List I (Phenomenon)List II (Examples)
A. Oestrus cycle(i) Strobilanthus kunthiana
B. Menstrual cycle(ii) Honeybees and turkey
C. Mass flowering once in 12 years(iii) Cows, sheep, and rats
D. Parthenogenesis(iv) Monkeys, apes, and humans

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Analysis of Mammalian Reproductive Cycles
Females of placental mammals exhibit cyclical changes in the activities of ovaries, accessory ducts, and hormones during the reproductive phase. In non-primate mammals such as cows, sheep, rats, deer, dogs, and tigers, these cyclical changes are called the oestrus cycle, whereas in primates such as monkeys, apes, and humans, they are called the menstrual cycle.

Step 2: Analysis of Unusual Flowering and Parthenogenesis
Strobilanthus kunthiana (neelakuranji) exhibits an unusual flowering phenomenon by flowering once in 12 years. Parthenogenesis is the development of a female gamete into a new organism without fertilisation, observed in rotifers, honeybees, some lizards, and birds such as turkey.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: Oestrus cycle with cows, sheep, and rats; Menstrual cycle with monkeys, apes, and humans; Mass flowering once in 12 years with Strobilanthus kunthiana; and Parthenogenesis with honeybees and turkey (A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(ii)).

name.text: NEETUG_BIOLOGY_REPRODUCTIONINORGANISMS_MATCHLIST_Q07 - Events and structures in sexual reproduction

questiontext.text:
Match List I with List II regarding key terms and events in sexual reproduction, and select the correct combination.

List I (Term / Event)List II (Description)
A. Homogametes(i) Thick protective wall of fruit developed from ovary
B. Syngamy(ii) Morphologically similar gametes as seen in Cladophora
C. Embryogenesis(iii) Fusion of male and female gametes to form a diploid zygote
D. Pericarp(iv) Development of embryo from zygote via mitosis and cell differentiation

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Pre-fertilisation and Fertilisation Concepts
In some algae such as Cladophora, the two gametes are so similar in appearance that they cannot be categorised into male and female gametes; these are called homogametes (isogametes). The fusion of male and female gametes, resulting in the formation of a diploid zygote, is called syngamy (or fertilisation).

Step 2: Post-fertilisation Concepts
Embryogenesis refers to the development of an embryo from the zygote, during which the zygote undergoes mitotic cell divisions to increase cell number and cell differentiation to form specialised tissues and organs. In flowering plants, after fertilisation, the ovary develops into the fruit, which forms a thick, protective wall called the pericarp.

Step 3: Final Conclusion
The correct pairings are: Homogametes with morphologically similar gametes as seen in Cladophora, Syngamy with fusion of male and female gametes to form a diploid zygote, Embryogenesis with development of embryo from zygote via mitosis and cell differentiation, and Pericarp with thick protective wall of fruit developed from ovary (A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(iv), D-(i)).
